title: SGLT2 inhibitors activate pantothenate kinase in the human heart.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I retrieved the Crossref record, the Europe PMC core record (isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions), the open bioRxiv preprint full text (doi 10.1101/2024.07.26.605401), and its data availability statement verbatim: 'All data supporting the findings of this study are available within the paper and its Supplementary Information.' I searched for deposits and found none: Zenodo (2 unrelated hits for PANK1, both breast-cancer target lists), Dryad (0 hits), OSF (0 hits), Metabolomics Workbench (no matching study; the only pantothenate study is ST003523 from Helsinki, unrelated), MassIVE (endpoint 404), and NCBI links from the PubMed record (no GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample or dbGaP entries). The bioRxiv supplement listing shows exactly one file, a PDF of supplemental figures (605401_file02.pdf); three download attempts returned HTTP 429 rate-limit, so I did not open it. science.org returns HTTP 403 for both the article and the supplementary-material path, so the published supplement is paywalled.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All experimental detail: ex vivo perfusion of human cardiac tissue blocks (average >40 g) from failing transplant-recipient hearts and non-failing organ-donor hearts with stable-isotope-labelled fuels; metabolite and acyl-coenzyme-A measurements; purified-PANK1 (pantothenate kinase 1) enzyme assays with empagliflozin and the known activator PZ-2891; 5 milliseconds of aggregate molecular dynamics of the unliganded PANK1 dimer run on Folding@home followed by docking and Markov state modelling; human cardiomyocyte contractility measurements. No sample counts, compound counts or measurement tables were visible to me because every number lives in figure panels.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified by searching repositories rather than by reading the paper. There is no deposited dataset anywhere: zero accessions in the record, zero hits on Zenodo/Dryad/OSF/Metabolomics Workbench, no GEO/SRA/BioProject links from PubMed. The data availability statement says everything is 'within the paper and its Supplementary Information', and the published Supplementary Information is a paywalled PDF (science.org returns 403); the preprint's equivalent is a single figure PDF with no tables.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. No table exists, so no column exists. Any label (for example, does a compound activate PANK1, or does empagliflozin change a metabolite level) would have to be read off figure panels by hand or re-derived from scratch.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. Features would have to be built from outside the paper entirely: chemical structures of the SGLT2 inhibitors (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors) from PubChem, the PANK1 sequence or structure from UniProt/PDB. Nothing is distributed with the paper.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in the text where numbers appear (700 nM empagliflozin, grams of tissue, 5 ms aggregate simulation), but this is from the paper only; there are no data files in which to check units.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. This is a mechanism paper: a handful of SGLT2 inhibitors, a few purified-enzyme dose-response curves, tens of perfused human heart blocks and cardiomyocyte preparations. Far below the ~1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires, and I could not even count them because they are only in figures.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; the only large object is the Folding@home molecular dynamics ensemble (5 ms aggregate for a PANK1 dimer in explicit solvent), which would be terabytes of trajectory data
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL in the only version of the project with real volume. The simulation ensemble is the one sizeable asset, it was never released, and raw trajectories at that scale exceed the 5 GB working-set limit and the 50 MB download limit by orders of magnitude.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: FAIL by impossibility, not by disagreement: there is no download and no application programming interface record to compare the paper's counts against.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying measurements are genuine physical assays (mass-spectrometry metabolite and acyl-coenzyme-A levels, enzyme kinetics, contractility), not another model's output. This is the one killer the paper would pass cleanly if the data were released; the predicted binding pose from docking would be a model output and must not be used as a label.

existing_models.name: CrypTothML (2025, International Journal of Molecular Sciences) — a method that finds cryptic, transiently-open drug pockets by combining mixed-solvent molecular dynamics with a machine-learning ranker
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by the authors as AUC-ROC (area under the receiver-operating curve) 0.88 on a curated cryptic-site benchmark; split details not checked because this paper failed Part A before the audit mattered.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not read; only the search abstract was retrieved.

backbone.name: none applicable — no data to fit a head on; ESM-2 (a protein language model) and ChemBERTa (a molecule language model) would both be plausible if a dataset existed

integration.partner_dataset: none viable; PDB and AlphaFold DB hold PANK1 structures and PubChem holds the SGLT2 inhibitor structures, but the paper contributes no rows to join them to
integration.join_key: UniProt accession Q8TE04 (PANK1) / InChIKey, in principle
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with a handful of compounds against one enzyme there is no combination that answers a question neither resource answers alone.

controls.positive_control: In an imagined version of this project, PZ-2891 (a published PANK activator named in the paper) would be the compound a working model must rank as an activator; no data exists to run it.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is not runnable — there are no labels in machine-readable form.
controls.external_validation: None. No second dataset of PANK1 activators exists that I found, and the paper's own measurements are not released.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is available, because no model can be trained: the paper reports a handful of experiments on one enzyme and a few drugs, all of it inside figure panels in a paywalled PDF.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use drug chemical structure to predict whether a compound activates pantothenate kinase 1, the enzyme that starts coenzyme A synthesis.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model each small molecule's chemical structure plus the shape of the enzyme pocket it sits in, and ask whether the compound speeds the enzyme up. The number of examples this paper offers is roughly five to ten compounds — unknown exactly, because every value is drawn in a figure.
plain_idea.predict: Activation of PANK1 as a yes/no or a fold-change. The true answer comes from purified-enzyme kinase assays run in this paper (two assay formats, drug added at nanomolar concentrations).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Heart-failure pharmacologists would use a reliable PANK1-activator predictor to design cleaner drugs than the SGLT2 inhibitors, which hit the kidney transporter as well. But that payoff needs hundreds of measured compounds, and this paper provides a handful.

ml_idea: The only idea the paper supports is a PANK1 (pantothenate kinase 1) allosteric-activator predictor, or reuse of the Folding@home conformational ensemble to learn where cryptic pockets open. Both die on data: the activator set is a handful of compounds measured only in figure panels, and the 5-millisecond simulation ensemble was never deposited. If the authors later release the trajectories, the pocket-opening question becomes interesting again, but it would need a graphics processing unit and terabytes of storage, not a laptop.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no file to size, so every compute figure would be invented.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement, which I did in the open preprint — it says all data are inside the paper and its Supplementary Information, and no repository search turns up a deposit. That one sentence kills the project in two minutes.

verdict_reason: No downloadable dataset exists (A1): the data availability statement keeps everything inside a paywalled Supplementary Information PDF, and Zenodo, Dryad, OSF, Metabolomics Workbench, GEO, SRA and BioProject all return nothing for this paper. Even if the PDF were open, this is a mechanism paper with a handful of compounds and tens of tissue samples, so A5 (enough rows) and A2 (label already a column) fail too.
